cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Every Glitch Is a Gift
cards.instruction: Turn every contradiction or failure into a surprising benefit of the impossible system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office clock is taking us backward. Leave it running; I intend to arrive at that meeting on time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've gone past the invitation. Can I stop it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. We have preparation time now. Bring me the agenda when it exists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're before the booking. The boss is asking me whether we need the meeting. What do I say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her I've decided we don't. This clock has cleared everyone's afternoon. Put that in your reply, and copy me so she knows who to thank.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 withholds permission to stop because the overshoot is preparation time; A5 dictates a decision to B boss, placing A above the nominal hierarchy through the next clock benefit.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 pre-invitation timing causes A3 waiting for agenda; B4 pre-booking consultation causes A5 cancelling and requesting credit.

relationship.evidence: B2 reasonably proposes stopping an overshoot; B4 asks how to answer the boss, materially changing A available intervention.

heightening.evidence: A5 upgrades B4 booking choice into clearing everyone afternoon and naming A as the decider, developing both optimism and assumed top status.

specificity.evidence: A1 office clock and meeting plus B4 boss establish workplace stakes without needing names or a physical time machine description.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 agenda when it exists is a concise response to reverse time; A5 copying A for credit follows the decision rather than another joke.
